subject: using pcountOpen to detect changes in apparent survival

messages.author: 5a86443c213d2d49
messages.subject: using pcountOpen to detect changes in apparent survival
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run some simulations to estimate the power to detect changes in stream amphibian abundance due to dam construction using a BACI design, and I am a little stuck with parameterizing the pcountOpen model.

This is a study that will run for 5 years, with 2 seasons Before and 3 seasons After dam construction, and will sample 50 sites (25 above and 25 below dams) at 5 facilities (5 sites above and below at each dam). We planning for 3 repeat visits per year at each site, which will consist of Time Constrained Searches to record larval abundance. We consider the sites 'closed' within a year (although there could be changes due to emigration/immigration), but 'open' among years. 

Given this dynamics, we decided that the data gathered will be used in pcountOpen for detecting potential population changes by testing for the Before/After Control/Impact interaction in the recruitment and apparent survival terms (similar to a study we performed using dynamic occupancy models, where we tested for the BACI interaction in the extinction and colonization terms; Popescu et al (2012) Ecol Apps 22:1389-1404). I simulating abundance data with high yearly survival and complementary recruitment rate (for population stationarity) and an impact on apparent survival (from season to season, not within season) during the After period at the Impact (below dam) sites.

The simulated datasets look good, but the models do not seem to be able to detect even drastic decreases in apparent survival (80%). I wonder if the problem is with the way I am setting the Before/After and Control/Impact variables (see below). I set them in a similar manner with colext, where 5 years require 4 transitions (1 column for Before, since there are 2 Before years, and 3 columns for After; with transition between Yr2 and Yr3 being the first After period). The last column is being ignored. Or should I do B for the first 2 years and A for the last 3?

SiteType   Yr1   Yr2  Yr3  Yr4  Yr5
-------------------------------------------------------
Impct        B      A     A    A     None                    # this is for 25 Impact sites
Ctrl           B      A     A    A     None                    # this is for 25 Control sites

I am using the Before/After setup as yearlySiteCovs, and SiteType as siteCovs.

The pcountOpen model (see below) fails to correctly estimate the simulated decrease in survival, and this points to 2 potential issues: (1) either the BACI variables are not setup correctly, or (2) apparent survival is estimated WITHIN, not between years (in which case the pcountOpen model might not be appropriate for our problem). Is there a way to differentiate between within- and among-year survival? Any thoughts on this would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you

Cheers,
Viorel


#### Simulation and Analysis R code ###################################### 


# s=apparent survival Before (Control and Impact sites) and After (Control sites only)
# sA=apparent survival After at Impact sites only
# p=detection probability
# siteT=number of Impact sites
# yearB=number of years Before
# yearA=number of years After
# nyear=total number of years (primary periods)
# n_vis=number of visits per year (secondary periods)


dataset <- function(sA, s=0.9, nyear=5, n_sites=50, n_vis=3, p=0.8, siteT=25, 
                    yearB=2, yearA=nyear-yearB) {
  
  tab <- matrix(rep(0, nyear*n_sites), ncol=nyear)        # matrix for storing true abundance values
  tab <- as.data.frame(tab)
  names(tab) <- paste("t", 1:nyear, sep="")
  
  obsab <- matrix(rep(0, nyear*n_sites*n_vis), ncol=(nyear*n_vis),
                   dimnames=list(paste("site", 1:n_sites, sep=""), paste("Yr", rep(1:nyear, each=n_vis), "v", 1:n_vis, sep="")))
  obsab <- as.data.frame(obsab)                                # matrix for storing observed abundance values
  
# simulate true and observed abundances

  for (i in 1:n_sites) {
    
    tab[i,1] = rnbinom(1, size=2.31, mu=6.70)                    # Simulate true abundance at t1 using a negative binomial distribution

    obsab[i,1:n_vis] = rbinom(n_vis, tab[i,1], p)                   # Simulate observed abundance at t1 using detection prob. p
    
    for(t in 2:nyear) {
      tab[i,t] <- rbinom(1,tab[i,t-1],s) + round(tab[i,t-1]*(1-s))  # abundance in subsequent years depends on apparent survival and recruitment
                                                                                     # we assume population stationarity
      
          for(j in 1:n_vis) {
            obsab[i,((t-1)*n_vis)+j] = rbinom(1, tab[i, t], p)         # observed data incorporates detection probability
          }
    }
  }
 
  ### Then simulate the Treatment sites After Impact portion of the tab and obsab matrices
  ### use the After (assumed) parameter values at Treatment Impacted sites only.
  ### The structure is similar to the previous Site 'for' loop

  for(i in 1:siteT) {                 # use the Treatment sites only
    
    for(tt in (yearB+1):nyear) {
      tab[i,tt] <- rbinom(1,tab[i,tt-1],sA) + round(tab[i,tt-1]*(1-s))          # abundance in subsequent years depends on apparent survival and recruitment
      
      for(j in 1:n_vis) {
        obsab[i,((tt-1)*n_vis)+j] = rbinom(1, tab[i, tt], p)   # observed data incorporates detection probability
      }
    }
  }
  
  ### Add a column to observed data for site type (Control or Treatment)
  obsab$treat = factor(c(rep('TRT', siteT), rep('CTRL', n_sites-siteT)))
  
  ### Create a matrix of yearly site covariates containing factors Before and After
  years.Before = matrix(rep("Before", n_sites*(yearB-1)), ncol=(yearB-1))
  years.After = matrix(rep("After", n_sites*yearA), ncol=yearA)
  years.None = matrix(rep("None", n_sites*1), ncol=1)
  years.BA = cbind(years.Before, years.After, years.None)
  years.BA = as.data.frame(years.BA)
  colnames(years.BA) <- paste("Yr", rep(1:nyear), sep="")
    
  ### Combine the observed P/A data and the yearly covariates (Years)
  obsab1=cbind(obsab, years.BA)
    
  return(data.frame(cbind(obsab1)))
}

require(unmarked)

analysis = function(Cdata, s=0.9, nyear=5, n_sites=50, n_vis=3, p=0.8, siteT=25, 
                    yearB=2, yearA=nyear-yearB) {
  
  
  
  #####################################################################
  ### Prepare data for 'unmarked', Dail-Madsen model
  
  # prepare the matrix for observed data
  yMat = Cdata[,1:(nyear*n_vis)]
  
  # prepare the matrix for Before/After : B and A periods had to be introduced as yearlySiteCovs
  BAMat = Cdata[,((nyear*n_vis)+2):((nyear*n_vis)+1+nyear)]
  yearlies = data.frame(BA = matrix(t(BAMat)))
  
  # prepare the multi-year pcountOpen data.frame
  umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(
    y=yMat, 
    siteCovs=Cdata[,"treat", drop=F],
    yearlySiteCovs=yearlies,
    numPrimary=nyear)
  
  ### Run 2 models
  Null.fit <- pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~treat+BA, ~1, umf, mixture="NB", K=50)
  Alt.fit <- pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~treat*BA, ~1, umf, mixture="NB", K=50)
  
  list(Null.fit = Null.fit, Alt.fit = Alt.fit)
}

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] using pcountOpen to detect changes in apparent survival
parts:
Hi Viorel,

For a study with 5 primary periods, there are 4 transitions, so you should have: B, B, A, A, NA; not B, A, A, A, NA. Also, I don't think that you are simulating data according to the default model (dynamics="constant"). For that model, the number of survivors is binomial, and the number of recruits is Poisson. There is an example on the help page. Hope this helps.

Richard
